records.statement: Squalene is commercially relevant in cosmetic and pharmaceutical sectors, and recent work emphasizes sustainable microbial production as an alternative to shark-derived sourcing.
records.notes: Industry/application context does not establish therapeutic efficacy of a consumer product.

records.statement: β-Carotene has long-standing commercial use as a food colorant and is available in multiple market forms for coloring food products.
records.notes: Industrial use is distinct from nutritional or therapeutic benefit.

records.statement: Myrcene is an industrially available renewable terpene feedstock whose unsaturated hydrocarbon chemistry supports diverse fine-chemical transformations and product classes.
records.notes: Industrial versatility is a chemistry/application claim, not evidence of a human health benefit.

records.statement: Limonene is a renewable bioeconomy chemical used in flavor, fragrance and solvent applications and as a platform/feedstock for higher-value products.
records.notes: Industrial use and renewability do not establish therapeutic efficacy or universal environmental superiority.

records.statement: α-Pinene has established flavor/fragrance relevance and is used as a renewable chemical scaffold for derivative synthesis and as an analytical target in essential-oil authenticity work.
records.notes: Application context does not convert historical use or derivative research into a therapeutic claim for α-pinene itself.

records.statement: Linalool is an established fragrance material with a dedicated fragrance-ingredient safety review.
records.notes: Fragrance use is documented here separately from sensory perception, biological research, and safety conclusions.

records.statement: β-Caryophyllene is used in fragrance applications and has been evaluated within the RIFM fragrance-ingredient safety framework.
records.notes: Fragrance application is distinct from receptor pharmacology, therapeutic use, or cannabis-effect claims.
